ei.title: Reading1 — Psychology — Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs
ei.subject: ReadingExpert5

fullPassage: What are the basic requirements of life and what do we need next after those? When you answer these questions, you’re doing the same kind of work that American psychologist Abraham Maslow did in his “hierarchy of needs” theory. The theory states that we must progress through various levels, satisfying the needs of each before being able to move on to the next. He thought individuals could eventually fulfill their potential if they could just satisfy several fundamental needs. The most basic needs form the bottom of Maslow’s hierarchy and are referred to as physiological needs. Physiological needs include our needs for food and shelter. Unless these are satisfied, we cannot move to the next level, safety needs. We need to feel secure in our environment, and this feeling of security usually means protection and freedom from fear. The third level is the need for love and belonging. People satisfy this need through their families and homes, as well as by joining and forming groups, making friends, and being part of a team. In the fourth level, the need for esteem refers to people’s need to be recognized. Here, they want to feel that others think highly of them; they may need praise and want to feel good about themselves. They may try to accomplish this by achieving set goals. Self-actualization, the fifth level, is the summit of Maslow’s hierarchy of needs. It is the quest to reach one’s full human potential. In this process people tend to have needs such as truth, justice, wisdom, and spiritual fulfillment. Despite the appealing logic of Maslow’s hierarchy, it seems to have some limits. Extensive research has suggested that there is little evidence for the ranking of levels and the argument of a definite hierarchy. Moreover, the concept of self-actualization is vague, and there’s no evidence to show that every individual can reach it. Maslow was the first psychologist to carry out academic research on human needs. He believed everybody should be encouraged to discover their vocations in life and endeavor to make life better. These are still important lessons today.

④ food: 음식 — 생리적 욕구라 존중 단계와 안 맞아요
det.tip: they may need ______ = 인정받고 싶어 칭찬(praise)이 필요함.

questions.passage: What are the basic requirements of life and what do we need next after those? When you answer these questions, you’re doing the same kind of work that American psychologist Abraham Maslow did in his “hierarchy of needs” theory. The theory states that we must progress through various levels, satisfying the needs of each before being able to move on to the next. He thought individuals could eventually fulfill their potential if they could just satisfy several <u>fundamental</u> needs. The most basic needs form the bottom of Maslow’s hierarchy and are referred to as physiological needs. Physiological needs include our needs for food and shelter. Unless these are satisfied, we cannot move to the next level, safety needs. We need to feel secure in our environment, and this feeling of security usually means protection and freedom from fear. The third level is the need for love and belonging. People satisfy this need through their families and homes, as well as by joining and forming groups, making friends, and being part of a team. In the fourth level, the need for esteem refers to people’s need to be recognized. Here, they want to feel that others think highly of them; they may need praise and want to feel good about themselves. They may try to accomplish this by achieving set goals. Self-actualization, the fifth level, is the summit of Maslow’s hierarchy of needs. It is the quest to reach one’s full human potential. In this process people tend to have needs such as truth, justice, wisdom, and spiritual fulfillment. Despite the appealing logic of Maslow’s hierarchy, it seems to have some limits. Extensive research has suggested that there is little evidence for the ranking of levels and the argument of a definite hierarchy. Moreover, the concept of self-actualization is vague, and there’s no evidence to show that every individual can reach it. Maslow was the first psychologist to carry out academic research on human needs. He believed everybody should be encouraged to discover their vocations in life and endeavor to make life better. These are still important lessons today.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 fundamental와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: fundamental=근본적인 / minor=사소한 / optional=선택적인 / temporary=일시적인 / essential=필수적인
det.analysis:
① minor: 사소한 — fundamental의 반대예요

② optional: 선택적인 — 꼭 필요한 것과 반대예요

③ temporary: 일시적인 — 지속성과 무관해요

④ essential: 필수적인 — fundamental(근본적인, 꼭 필요한)의 동의어 ←정답
det.tip: several fundamental needs = 몇 가지 필수적인 욕구 → essential.

det.korean: vague=모호한 / unclear=불분명한 / odd=이상한 / complex=복잡한 / clear=분명한
det.analysis:
① unclear: 불분명한 — vague와 비슷해 반의어가 아니에요

② odd: 이상한 — 의미축이 달라요

③ complex: 복잡한 — 모호함의 반대가 아니에요

④ clear: 분명한 — vague(모호한)의 반의어 ←정답
det.tip: the concept is vague ↔ clear(분명한).

questions.passage:
(A) This feeling of security usually <u>means</u> protection and freedom from fear.

(B) After years of saving, she finally had the <u>means</u> to travel around the world.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)에서 밑줄 친 means의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: means: (A) 의미하다, 뜻하다 (B) 수단, 재력
det.analysis:
① (A) 수단 (B) 의미하다: (A)는 안전감이 보호를 '의미한다'예요

② (A) 의미하다 (B) 수단: 안전감이 보호를 '의미하다' + 여행할 '수단(재력)' ←정답

③ (A) 평균 (B) 의미하다: (A)는 평균이 아니에요

④ (A) 의미하다 (B) 비열한: (B)는 형용사 '비열한'이 아니라 명사 '수단'이에요
det.tip: security means protection = 의미하다 vs the means to travel = 수단.

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a system in which people or things are arranged according to their rank or importance"

det.korean: democracy=민주주의 / boundary=경계 / hierarchy=위계, 계층 구조 / routine=일상
det.analysis:
① democracy: 민주주의 — 다수결 통치라 서열 배열과 달라요

② boundary: 경계 — 경계선이라 서열이 아니에요

③ hierarchy: 위계 — 사람·사물을 중요도·서열에 따라 배열한 체계 ←정답

④ routine: 일상 — 반복되는 절차라 의미가 달라요
det.tip: arranged according to rank or importance → 위계(hierarchy).

questions.passage: The most basic needs form the bottom of Maslow's hierarchy and are __________ (refer) to as physiological needs. Physiological needs include our needs for food and shelter.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: refer → referred: 'are + __________ + to as'는 수동태라 과거분사(p.p.)로 바꿔요.
det.analysis:
'are __________ to as physiological needs(~로 불린다)'에서 be동사(are) 뒤 자리라 수동태예요.

→ 가장 기본적인 욕구가 '~라고 불리는' 대상이니 수동의 과거분사가 필요해요.

→ 원형 refer를 과거분사 referred로 바꿔요.
det.tip: are referred to as ~ = ~라고 불린다 (수동태 be + p.p.).

questions.passage: Maslow was the first psychologist to carry out academic research on human needs. He believed everybody should be __________ (encourage) to discover their vocations in life and endeavor to make life better.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: encourage → encouraged: 'should be + __________'는 수동태라 과거분사(p.p.)로 바꿔요.
det.analysis:
'everybody should be __________ to discover(모두가 ~하도록 격려받아야 한다)'에서 조동사 다음 be동사 뒤 자리라 수동태예요.

→ 모두가 '격려받는' 대상이니 수동의 과거분사가 필요해요.

→ 원형 encourage를 과거분사 encouraged로 바꿔요.
det.tip: should be encouraged = 격려받아야 한다 (수동태 be + p.p.).
